newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway has no plans to join Danish-Swedish bourse.
newsitem.headline: Norway has no plans to join Danish-Swedish bourse.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange has no immediate plans to join a joint share-trading system agreed by the bourses of neighbouring Sweden and Denmark, director Kjell Froensdal said on Thursday.

He said the agreement between Stockholm and Copenhagen, which may boost the combined bourses' turnover by at least 10 percent and eventually lead to a pan-Nordic securities market, was "positive and visionary".
"I congratulate them, but we have set our own course on a trading platform for shares, which means it is of no interest for us to join this cooperation at the moment," Froensdal told Reuters.
Speaking at a news conference in Copenhagen, Danish bourse president Lars Johansen said that the joint trading system with Stockholm should be operating by the summer of 1998 at the earliest.
Johansen said that the new partners had invited the Finnish, Icelandic and Norwegian bourses to join the alliance.

Froensdal said cooperation was technically possible once Oslo's new trading platform was in place, but it was unlikely in the near future because Sweden and Denmark had decided to adopt Stockholm's SAX system.
The Oslo exchange announced two weeks ago it had entered final negotiations with Australia's Computer-share Systems Limited (CSL) on a new computer system for trading in equities.
It is scheduled to start operating by 1998, providing users with an automatch system as opposed to the current system where orders are matched manually by phone.
Decentralised, off-floor trade will allow for overseas brokers to become members of the Oslo Bourse, one of the smallest in Europe.
